rationale_by_issue.iti13:3.1: The bracketed identical-verses summary describes the omitted verse, not the closing prose colophon; begin it on the first verse line.
rationale_by_issue.dhp113:2: The unseen rise/fall qualification belongs to Pali line2; the single-day comparison and its seeing qualification belong to lines3 and4 respectively.
rationale_by_issue.dhp170:2: The mirage simile belongs to Pali line2, before the world-regarding clause at line3.
rationale_by_issue.dhp257:3: The unhurried/Dhamma method belongs to lines1–2, while guarding/intelligence begins line3; English reverses the first pair, so keep it grouped at line1 and start line3 at guarding.
rationale_by_issue.iti33:3.4: English reorders person/discerning and endowed-with-two-things relative to Pali3.3–3.5; group the complete condition at its first covered line3.3, leaving rebirth separate at3.6.
rationale_by_issue.an4.195:3.1: The temporal connector 'when' opens the following Buddha-arrival clause rather than ending the unfinished-conversation statement.
rationale_by_issue.an4.10:4.3: The repeated not-discerning condition renders the appajānato clause on4.3, not the first uncomprehending statement on4.2.
rationale_by_issue.an4.10:8.3: The repeated discerning condition renders pajānato on8.3, not the preceding statement on8.2.
rationale_by_issue.iti74:6.2: The child object precedes the wise-person predicate in Pali but follows it in English; keep the inseparable reversed sentence at its first Pali line6.1.
rationale_by_issue.an5.43:9.1: Verse list and qualifiers are shifted by two lines: life/beauty/status/honor belong9.1, heaven/highbirth9.2, aspiration9.3, and great/repeated9.4.
rationale_by_issue.iti76:3.2: Original Pali places guarding virtue3.1, aspiring to three happinesses3.2, praise/wealth3.3, and heaven after death3.4; English has separable clauses for all four.
rationale_by_issue.iti76:7.2: English reverses the wrapping subject and object relative to Pali7.1–7.2; group the complete clause at7.1.
rationale_by_issue.iti76:8.2: English reverses the wrapping subject and object relative to Pali8.1–8.2; group the complete clause at8.1.
rationale_by_issue.iti76:9.2: English knowing/outcome precedes the leaf-wrapper simile while Pali orders them inversely; group the complete clause at9.1.
rationale_by_issue.snp4.7:1.1: The first utterance covers the sexual-intercourse condition at1.1 as well as the request at1.3; its interlocutor heading is between them. Preserve source order by grouping at the first covered Pali line1.1.
rationale_by_issue.snp4.7:10.2: The closing verse reverses the people-who-envy and the remote-sage/flood-crossing descriptions relative to Pali; preserve its source order by grouping all four lines at10.1.
rationale_by_issue.sn35.229:3.4: Sharks and demons translate sagāhaṁ sarakkhasaṁ on3.3; only waves and difficulty of crossing begin3.4.
rationale_by_issue.sn35.229:4.2: Acquisition-free translates nirupadhi on4.1 but English places it after abandoning stress on4.2; group the reordered pair at4.1.
rationale_by_issue.sn12.31:2.4: The question's astute/manner-of-life line and asked/tell/address line are reversed/overlapping in English; preserve its complete two-line request at2.3.
rationale_by_issue.sn12.31:5.4: The repeated question's manner-of-life object belongs5.3 but follows asked/tell on5.4 in English; group the pair at5.3.
rationale_by_issue.sn12.31:9.4: Same reordered question as2.3–2.4; group its whole request at9.3.
rationale_by_issue.sn42.8:6.4: The independent thought-arising clause translates tassa evaṁ hoti on6.4, following the faith-in-teacher statement on6.3.
rationale_by_issue.sn42.8:7.7: The reflection predicate translates so iti paṭisañcikkhati on7.7 and can stand after the preceding faith-in-teacher clause.
rationale_by_issue.thag13.1:7.3: The One-with-Eyes epithet from7.4 is moved next to the Teacher at7.2 before the lute simile7.3; preserve the reordered subject/predicate unit at7.2, clearing7.3 and7.4.
rationale_by_issue.thag13.1:11.4: English reverses nothing-to-do (Pali11.4) and nothing-to-add (Pali11.3); group the pair at11.3.
rationale_by_issue.an8.13:2.11: The purpose/result clause about companions straightening faults belongs2.11 and separates naturally from revealing faults on2.10.
rationale_by_issue.iti112:9.2: English moves awakened (buddho) from Pali9.1 after trouble (anīgho) from9.2; group the reordered description at9.1.
rationale_by_issue.an10.104:2.5: Original Pali2.4 includes bodily and verbal actions after the wrong-view list;2.5 begins mental actions. Move the English body/verbal clauses back to2.4.
rationale_by_issue.an10.104:4.5: Original Pali4.4 includes bodily/verbal actions after the right-view list;4.5 begins mental actions. Split English at the same original-Pali boundary.
rationale_by_issue.an5.140:11.3: The causal relative connector by which (yatvādhikaraṇam) opens the unrestrained-eye consequence on11.3, rather than concluding the non-grasping statement on11.2. Quote crosses the currently split rows with normalized whitespace.
rationale_by_issue.an5.140:11.9: The parallel causal relative connector belongs the unrestrained-intellect consequence on11.9, rather than the preceding non-grasping statement. Quote crosses the currently split rows with normalized whitespace.
rationale_by_issue.an5.200:6.2: The lack-of-obsession conditions translate the second half of Pali6.1;6.2 begins only with calling him a monk without attachment (ayaṁ vuccati...). Move the separable causal list back to6.1.
rationale_by_issue.dhp284:2: English places the least-bit qualifier (Pali2) before the not-cleared predicate (Pali1); group the intertwined condition at line1.
rationale_by_issue.dhp321:4: English reverses enduring accusation (Pali4) and being best among humans (Pali3); group the complete description at line3.

coverage_and_source_variant_concerns.note: The prose of several consecutive discourses is combined under Iti10; Iti13 has only a verses-summary note. These are source condensation/coverage issues, not missing-English boundary errors.

The long opening narrative is expanded in the English where this Pali layout abbreviates its opening topic list; retain translator words without claiming separate exact Pali matches for all narrative clauses.
The final bride/newly ordained simile is omitted by this translation; empty9.x rows are genuine source omissions.
Verse4.3 English 'has no measure' differs from appended Pali 'na puneti' (does not return). This is source/translation wording, not a displaced boundary.

The English concludes its quotation-introduction with the understanding statement before quoting, whereas original Pali concludes after quoting at10.1/14.1. Preserve this source restructuring; do not treat the empty closing wrapper as omitted quoted material.

At16.3 English adds 'safe' before 'consummate in knowledge'; appended Pali16.4 has sottiyo. This may reflect the sotthiyo/sottiyo reading or translator interpretation, so it is not counted as a clear displaced standalone boundary.

At13.10 the English says long-term harm/suffering while appended Pali reads hitāya sukhāya (benefit/happiness) after na piveyya; this looks like a source-text reading problem rather than an alignment shift.
English source labels this discourse78 while the Pali/Sujato key is77; content matches.
English3.3 says ten-thousand-fold cosmos while Pali has sahassī (thousandfold); content otherwise belongs the right key.

scope_note: Findings are review proposals only. No translation data, cuts, scripts, app, or main integration files were changed; no commit was made.
denominator_note: All 1,819 displayed Pali/English rows were read, including 11 Dhammapada :0 story headings. The non-title count excludes those :0 or 0.* keys but includes numbered 1.0 rows and untranslated colophons/uddana; English-empty rows remain in the read denominator.
quote_validation: Every starts quote occurs literally in normalized same-text concatenation of displayed T fields. A few whole short phrases use fewer than six words; causal-connector quotes cross an existing row boundary.
